resolved_target_definition.label: Moral hazard
candidate_definitions: Moral hazard arises when protection from a loss changes incentives to avoid it. An insured business might invest less in theft prevention because an insurer bears part of the cost. Deductibles leave some losses with the policyholder, potentially preserving incentives for care.

Moral hazard describes how protection from consequences can change behavior after an agreement. Insurance may reduce the incentive to prevent a loss when another party pays much of the cost. Insurers use monitoring and cost sharing to address this problem, although they cannot observe every risky action.

relationship_checks.assessment: The baseline moral-hazard cards use insurance examples, not another homonymous concept. The paper explicitly identifies its multiagent case as moral hazard.
